turnaround_reason: Everforth, a Glen Allen VA digital-engineering/IT-services firm (~$3.97B TTM revenue, ~2,800 employees), fell from ~$55 to a $16.9 low on slowing growth and margin compression; it has since rebounded to ~$32 but forward growth is only ~2% and the re-rating case is thin.
bullish_points: Cheap on forward earnings (fwd PE ~7.5) with a large, established revenue base (~$3.97B TTM)
Q2 CY2026 beat: revenue topped estimates by ~1.6% and EPS beat by ~36%, with optimistic next-quarter sales guidance
Stock has already reclaimed its trend (trading ~134% of the 100d MA), suggesting the base may be in
dossier shows modest insider purchase activity and options exist, giving some optionality
bearish_points: Growth is anemic: revenue forecast ~2.3% annually vs ~14% for the US IT industry — this is a slow-grower, not a re-accelerating turnaround
Profitability is deteriorating: Q2 net income down 52% YoY, EPS $0.35 vs $0.67 prior year
Options are effectively illiquid (sampled ATM IV ~0.001, thin OI) — spot-only, and the ticker/name is unfamiliar, adding due-diligence risk
High leverage (debt/equity ~83) against a shrinking-margin profile
catalyst: Margin stabilization and any acceleration in digital-engineering/AI-services demand that lifts the ~2% growth trajectory
catalyst_timing: Next quarterly print (roughly Oct-Nov 2026) and FY2027 guide
suggested_trade: Spot only, small starter if at all; a cheap-but-slow IT-services name that needs a growth or margin catalyst to re-rate
key_risk: IT-services margin compression continues and growth stays ~2%, so the low multiple is deserved and the stock dead-money
would_skip_if: Margins keep compressing or growth guidance stays low-single-digit; no clear catalyst to re-rate a slow-grower
